title: Security Scanning Exception Configuration
description: Documented false positives and reviewed security exceptions for secret and dependency scanning.

secretExceptions.reason: Simulated secret patterns used strictly in unit tests for negative security scanner testing.

dependencyExceptions.reason: Transitive sub-dependency of postcss; custom generator size=0 edge case is unused in application/build code paths.
Transitive dev-dependency of ESLint config (@eslint/eslintrc); maxTotalMergeKeys CPU consumption on empty merge sources does not affect runtime applications as no untrusted YAML is parsed.

Platform-specific RCE restricted to Windows-hosted servers; staging and production runtime environments strictly run on containerized Linux (node:20-alpine / Railway PaaS), rendering Windows path traversal unexploitable.

Next.js Image Optimization API RCE triggered by AVIF files; application does not configure AVIF image formats, uses zero external image uploads, and relies strictly on static SVGs and remote avatars from approved Google/Pinterest origins.
Vulnerabilities in libheif decoder bundled in sharp sub-dependency; application processes only numerical IoT telemetry and does not ingest or decode HEIF/HEIC image assets.

Transitive sub-dependency of Fastify (@fastify/ajv-compiler, ajv, fast-json-stringify); authority injection and host confusion vulnerabilities in fast-uri URI serialization are unexploitable as all incoming API and IoT Gateway routes use strict static schemas without parsing untrusted external URI authority components.

Transitive dev-dependency of ESLint and @typescript-eslint (@eslint/eslintrc, minimatch, glob); DoS via uncontrolled recursion on nested brace groups or parseCommaParts causing stack exhaustion is restricted to build/lint time and does not affect runtime applications as no untrusted user input is parsed.

Next.js RCE in next/og ImageResponse; application does not use next/og or ImageResponse anywhere in the codebase, processes only structured numerical IoT telemetry, and relies strictly on static SVGs and monogram initials.

Transitive dev-dependency of Tailwind CSS (@next/eslint-plugin-next, fast-glob, micromatch, chokidar); stack-exhaustion DoS via deeply nested patterns (GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm) is restricted to build/lint time and does not affect runtime applications as no untrusted user input is parsed.
Transitive dev-dependency of Tailwind CSS and fast-glob flagged solely due to sub-dependency braces; used strictly at build/lint time with no runtime exposure.
Transitive dev-dependency of Tailwind CSS flagged solely due to sub-dependency braces; used strictly for local build file-watching with no runtime exposure.
Transitive dev-dependency of ESLint and Tailwind CSS flagged solely due to sub-dependency micromatch/braces; used strictly at build/lint time with no runtime exposure.
Dev-dependency of eslint-config-next flagged solely due to transitive sub-dependency fast-glob/micromatch/braces; used strictly at build/lint time with no runtime exposure.

Vulnerability in librsvg dependency (CVE-2026-96889) bundled in sharp sub-dependency; application processes only structured numerical IoT telemetry and static bundled assets, and does not ingest or rasterize untrusted user SVG assets.

Event-loop denial of service via indexed source-map section offsets (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q); source-map-js is a dev-only and build-time transitive dependency of PostCSS/Tailwind CSS with zero production runtime exposure or parsing of untrusted source maps.
Transitive dev-dependency of Tailwind CSS flagged due to sub-dependency postcss-selector-parser; used strictly at build time for CSS compilation with no client or server production runtime exposure.
